sites.name: Alaska Mine
overview: Alaska Mine is a named historic gold-, silver-, and lead-bearing mine in Chaffee County, preserved on U.S. topographic mapping in the Garfield quadrangle near the Monarch mining area.

timeline.text: Alaska Mine became an established named mine locality in the Garfield quadrangle and was retained in federal topographic feature records.

moreHistory: USGS-derived mapped-place records locate Alaska Mine at approximately 38.55916, -106.27697 and about 10,266 feet elevation, and describe the inactive mine as associated with silver, gold, and lead.
Available site-specific records support the mine's identity and location but do not provide a dependable detailed operating chronology or production history.

sourceReferences.title: Alaska Mine Topo Map in Chaffee County, Colorado
sourceReferences.note: Identifies Alaska Mine in Chaffee County at 38.5591639, -106.2769674, gives an elevation of about 10,266 feet, describes it as an inactive silver, gold, and lead mine, and places it on the Garfield USGS quadrangle.

sourceReferences.title: Garfield-area mine feature listing
sourceReferences.publisher: TopoQuest / U.S. Geological Survey topographic data
sourceReferences.note: USGS-derived Garfield-quadrangle listing independently preserves Alaska Mine at approximately 38.559164, -106.276967 among nearby named mine features.

sites.name: Alderman Deposit
overview: Alderman Deposit is a federally documented fluorite-bearing mineral deposit in the Browns Canyon district of Chaffee County, developed by historic underground workings.

timeline.text: The Alderman deposit was developed by a crosscut adit and drift as part of mineral exploration and mining activity in the Browns Canyon district.
U.S. Geological Survey Professional Paper 626 documented the Alderman deposit and its underground workings in the Poncha Springs NE quadrangle.

moreHistory: USGS documentation identifies the Alderman deposit as a Browns Canyon fluorite locality and describes a roughly 210-foot crosscut adit reaching a drift about 90 feet long. The report noted that the adit was caved by the time of publication.
A later U.S. Geological Survey mineral-resource compilation retained the Alderman deposit at approximately 38.6253, -106.0661, preserving a stable location for this historic mineral property.

sourceReferences.title: Geology and mineral deposits of the Poncha Springs NE quadrangle, Chaffee County, Colorado — Professional Paper 626
sourceReferences.note: Documents the Alderman deposit in the Browns Canyon area and describes the crosscut adit and drift workings.

sourceReferences.title: Fluorine, Fluorite, and Fluorspar — Scientific Investigations Report 2010-5113
sourceReferences.note: Lists the Alderman deposit in Browns Canyon at approximately 38.6253, -106.0661.

sites.name: Allard Beryllium Mine
overview: Allard, also known as the Combination Prospect, is a federally documented beryllium-bearing pegmatite property in the Turret district. Federal and mapped locality evidence provides a defensible Basic Scan anchor without implying present condition.

timeline.text: USGS pegmatite investigations documented the Allard/Combination property during federal beryllium exploration of the Turret district.

sites.name: Alpha and Beta Mine
overview: Alpha and Beta is a named Monarch-district gold-silver mine preserved on federal topographic mapping. The mapped mine feature provides a stable Basic Scan identification anchor even though a richer site-specific operating chronology has not been recovered.

timeline.text: USGS-derived Garfield quadrangle mapping preserves Alpha and Beta as a named mine feature in the Monarch mining district.

sites.name: American Flag Mine
overview: American Flag is a documented Turret-district gold mine with Anaconda, Crete, Ethel Consolidation and Holdredge recorded as associated historical names.

sites.name: Anna Huffman Copper
overview: Anna Huffman is a named Chaffee County copper property with a documented 1952 federal exploration episode.

sites.name: Annie C Mine
overview: Annie C is a named historic gold-mine locality in Chaffee County's Free Gold district. Federal topographic mapping provides a stable identification point while unsupported operator or production details are intentionally omitted.

timeline.text: USGS-derived Buena Vista West quadrangle mapping preserves Annie C as a named mine feature associated with the Free Gold mining district.

sites.name: April Fool Mine (Chaffee County)
overview: April Fool is a documented Monarch-district lead-silver mine preserved on USGS topographic mapping.

sites.name: Atlantic / Mound / Independence
overview: Atlantic, Mound, and Independence are linked historical names for the same South Cottonwood mining property. The USGS-mapped Mound Mine feature provides a defensible site-level Basic Scan anchor.

timeline.text: Federal and locality records preserve Atlantic, Mound, and Independence as linked names for the same Chaffee County mining property.

sites.name: Bancroft
overview: Bancroft Mine is a distinct named USGS mine feature. The nearby Bancroft Incline is a separate mapped feature and is not conflated with this Basic Scan target.

timeline.text: USGS 1:24,000 mapping preserves Bancroft Mine as a distinct Chaffee County mine locality.

sites.name: Be True Mine
overview: Be True is a federally mapped Chaffee County uranium mine and past-producer locality. The named USGS mine feature supplies a stable Basic Scan anchor while uncertain operator, production, and surviving-remnant details remain unasserted.

timeline.text: USGS-derived Buena Vista West mapping and federal mine records preserve Be True as a named uranium mine and past producer.

sites.name: Ben Bolts Paymaster
overview: Ben Bolts Paymaster is a mapped Monarch-district silver mine and past-producer locality. Federal mapping and mine records support the identity and location for Basic Scan while richer operating history and present-day workings remain unasserted.

timeline.text: USGS-derived Garfield quadrangle mapping preserves Ben Bolts Paymaster as a named inactive silver mine in the Monarch district.

sites.name: Ben Boyer Claim
overview: Ben Boyer Claim is a uniquely mapped Cleora-district prospect locality suitable for site-level Basic Scan identification. No surviving open working is asserted.

timeline.text: Federal mineral-resource records preserve the Ben Boyer Claim as a named Cleora-district prospect locality.

sites.name: Ben Hill Mine
overview: Ben Hill is a documented Chaffee County lead-silver mine preserved as a named USGS topographic feature.

sites.name: Betsy
overview: Betsy Mine is preserved as a distinct named Chaffee County mine feature in USGS-derived mapping. The mapped point is used only as a site-level anchor and not as exact portal geometry.

timeline.text: USGS-derived Granite-quadrangle mapping preserves Betsy Mine as a named historic mine locality.

sites.name: Black Tiger Mine
overview: Black Tiger is a documented Monarch-district lead-silver mine. Colorado Geological Survey and USGS mapping provide a defensible site-level Basic Scan anchor without asserting present portal condition.

timeline.text: Historic federal and Colorado records preserve Black Tiger as a producing Monarch-area lode and mapped mine feature.

sites.name: Blue Brute Mine
overview: Blue Brute is a documented Turret-district beryllium prospect and mine property with two recorded open cuts. The mapped historic working area provides a defensible Basic Scan anchor without asserting current cut condition.

timeline.text: Federal DMEA and MRDS records preserve the Blue Brute claims, associated names, and documented open-cut workings.

sites.name: Blue Stone Deposit
overview: Blue Stone is a federally documented Browns Canyon fluorspar property with a shallow shaft, adit and surface cuts.

sites.name: Bonnie Belle Mine
overview: Bonnie Belle is a documented Monarch-district lead-silver mine preserved on the Garfield USGS quadrangle.

sites.name: Boss Lake Mine
overview: Boss Lake is a documented Chaffee County iron mine and magnetite stockpile locality.

sites.name: Brighton Mine (Chaffee County)
overview: The Chaffee County Brighton is a historic Monarch-area silver-lead producer distinct from same-name Colorado mines.

sites.name: Buckhorn Tunnel
overview: Buckhorn Tunnel is tied to a specific mapped underground working and federal Mine Map Repository record. The historical tunnel location supports Basic Scan without asserting current portal condition.

timeline.text: Federal mine-map records preserve Buckhorn Tunnel as a specific underground working in Chaffee County.

sites.name: Calumet Mine
overview: Calumet is a major historic Chaffee County iron mine with extensive documented workings and a strong railroad/company-town history. The federal MRDS main-entrance location provides a defensible Basic Scan anchor.

timeline.text: Calumet shipped iron ore over the Denver & Rio Grande branch and supplied Colorado Coal and Iron / CF&I before declining ore quality led to closure.

sites.name: Chimney Hill Mine
overview: Chimney Hill is a federally mapped Browns Canyon fluorspar mine with documented shaft, adit, level and pit workings.

sites.name: Cleora No. 2 Prospect
overview: Cleora No. 2 is a federally documented prospect developed by a 150-foot adit on the east side of Longfellow Gulch. The mapped historic adit location provides a defensible Basic Scan anchor.

timeline.text: USGS/MRDS documentation records a 150-foot adit at the Cleora No. 2 prospect.

sites.name: Clinton Mine (Chaffee County)
overview: Clinton is a documented Monarch-district mine with early-1880s development and later 1901-1904 production.

sites.name: Colorado-American Mine
overview: Colorado-American was the principal fluorspar producer of the Browns Canyon district and has extensive mapped surface and underground workings.

sites.name: Columbine Mine (Chaffee County)
overview: The Chaffee County Columbine Mine is independently mapped as a named mine locality. The locality is used for Basic Scan without asserting a surviving open portal or current working condition.

timeline.text: USGS/GNIS-derived mapping preserves Columbine Mine as a distinct Chaffee County mine locality.

sites.name: Columbus Mine
overview: Columbus Mine is a mapped Chaffee County mine locality associated historically with tunnel, shaft, and mill components. The parent mine locality is used as the Basic Scan anchor without claiming which component survives today.

timeline.text: USGS mapping and early Colorado mining records preserve the Columbus mining complex in the Monarch area.

sites.name: Copper King Lode
overview: Copper King Lode is a federally documented Chaffee County copper-gold vein property with a traceable claim and mineral-examination record.

sites.name: Crystal No. 8 Mine
overview: Crystal No. 8 is a federally documented pegmatite mine developed by a substantial two-level open cut and short adit.

sites.name: Darling Mine
overview: Darling is a documented Monarch-district silver-lead mine preserved on USGS topographic mapping.

sites.name: Delay Adit and Lloyd Shaft
overview: Delay Adit and Lloyd Shaft are linked but distinct historic workings in the Browns Canyon fluorspar district. Federal mapping provides a defensible site-level anchor for the combined working complex.

timeline.text: USGS Professional Paper 626 separately maps the Delay Adit and Lloyd Shaft workings within the Browns Canyon district.

sites.name: Eclipse Mine
overview: Eclipse is a documented Monarch-district zinc and lead mine with extensive historic underground workings.

sites.name: Elkington Mine
overview: Elkington is a documented Monarch-area lead-silver mine preserved as a named historic mine feature.

sites.name: Evening Star Mine (Chaffee County)
overview: Evening Star is a documented Monarch Hill mine with shaft, adit and extensive underground workings.

sites.name: Fairplay Mine
overview: Fairplay is a distinct Chaffee County lead-silver mine and past-producer locality.

sites.name: Fraction Mine (Chaffee County)
overview: Fraction is a documented Monarch-district lead-silver mine preserved on the Garfield USGS quadrangle.

sites.name: Futurity Mine
overview: Futurity is a documented Chaffee County copper-gold-silver mine associated with the Futurity–Bassam Ridge mining landscape. USGS-derived topographic locality data provides a stable mine-level Scan anchor.

timeline.text: State mining records document Futurity as a copper-producing property with gold and silver context.

sites.name: Garfield Mine
overview: Garfield Mine is a documented Taylor Gulch lead-zinc property with historic adit workings.

sites.name: Gladstone Mine
overview: Gladstone Mine is a distinct Chaffee County silver-lead past producer preserved in federal and Colorado mining records. The USGS-mapped mine locality provides a defensible Basic Scan anchor without asserting present portal condition.

timeline.text: Federal mineral-resource records and Colorado mining reports preserve Gladstone as a named Chaffee County underground mine.

sites.name: Gold Bug Mine (Turret District)
overview: Gold Bug is a documented Turret-district gold-silver mine with a deep shaft and substantial historic dump.

sites.name: Golden Age Mine
overview: Golden Age is a documented Monarch-district silver-lead mine with state and federal source support. USGS-derived topographic mapping provides a stable Basic Scan anchor.

timeline.text: Colorado Geological Survey and USGS records preserve Golden Age as a named Monarch-district producer.

sites.name: Golden Cache Mine (Chaffee County)
overview: Golden Cache is a documented Granite-district gold mine preserved as a named Chaffee County mine locality.

sites.name: Golden Wonder Mine
overview: Golden Wonder is a documented Turret-district gold mine with operating-era evidence and inclined workings.

sites.name: Grand View Mine
overview: Grand View is a documented Cleora-district mine complex developed by multiple adits and a shaft. The federal mine-complex locality provides a defensible Basic Scan anchor without asserting a currently open portal.

timeline.text: Federal records identify Grand View as a small copper-gold-tungsten operation discovered and first produced in 1890, with last recorded production in 1905.

sites.name: Great Monarch and Marshall Tunnel
overview: Great Monarch is one of the foundational 1878 discoveries of the Monarch district. The mapped Great Monarch mine feature provides a defensible parent Scan anchor while the Marshall Tunnel remains a related component.

timeline.text: The Great Monarch claim was discovered during the founding period of the Monarch mining district.

sites.name: Herskberger Tunnel
overview: Herskberger Tunnel is a named Turret-district historic gold mine preserved on USGS-derived mapping.

sites.name: Holy Water Mine
overview: Holy Water, also mapped as Holywater Mine, is a named Chaffee County gold-silver past-producer locality.

sites.name: Indianapolis Mine
overview: Indianapolis is a documented Taylor Gulch gold mine with a short adit and shallow winze.

sites.name: Iron Chest Mine (Gold Property, Chaffee County)
overview: This Iron Chest record is the gold-polymetallic Chalk Creek property, distinct from other same-name Chaffee occurrences. USGS production history and mapped mine locality support a defensible Basic Scan anchor.

timeline.text: USGS records most early production before 1900 and documented production episodes in 1902 and 1913–1915.

sites.name: Iron Duke Mine (Chaffee County)
overview: Iron Duke is a documented Monarch-district mine preserved on federal/topographic mapping.

sites.name: Jewell Tunnel
overview: Jewell Tunnel is a documented Monarch-area zinc and polymetallic mine with early-20th-century production and later federal exploration. Mapped locality evidence provides a stable Scan anchor.

timeline.text: State and federal records document production, development, examination, and rehabilitation work at Jewell Tunnel.

sites.name: Lienhart Mine
overview: Lienhart is a well-documented polymetallic mine with a dedicated Colorado Geological Survey site report and identified adit, waste-rock, and tailings components. USGS place mapping provides a stable parent anchor.

timeline.text: The Lienhart property, also known by several Mount Harvard-related names, was developed by an adit and associated surface mine features.

sites.name: Little Wonder Mine
overview: Little Wonder is a documented Monarch-area lead mine preserved as a named USGS mine feature.

sites.name: Madonna Mine
overview: Madonna is one of the principal historic mines of the Monarch district, with extensive multi-level workings and major zinc/lead-silver production. USGS topographic locality data provides a stable parent-mine Scan anchor.

timeline.text: Madonna was discovered in 1878 and became one of the Monarch district's principal long-running producers.

sites.name: Moss Flower (Half Moon Mine)
overview: Moss Flower is a named Chaffee County mine preserved on the Garfield USGS quadrangle; the Half Moon relationship remains retained as an associated property name rather than invented history.

sites.name: New York Mine
overview: New York is a documented Monarch-district gold mine with multiple federal Mine Map Repository references.

sites.name: Ohio and Morningstar Mine
overview: Ohio and Morningstar is a named Chaffee County gold-silver mine preserved on USGS topographic mapping.

sites.name: Paymaster Mine (Chaffee County)
overview: Paymaster is a documented Monarch-district lead-silver mine, distinct from same-name mines elsewhere in Colorado.

sites.name: Pride of the West Mine (Chaffee County)
overview: Pride of the West is a documented Chaffee County gold-silver mine preserved on USGS topographic mapping.

sites.name: Sedalia Mine
overview: Sedalia is a major historic copper-zinc mine with documented multi-adit development and a stable mapped mine locality.

sites.name: Shamrock Mine (Chaffee County)
overview: Shamrock is a documented Monarch-district gold mine with copper, lead, and silver mineralization. Its mapped mine locality provides a defensible Basic Scan anchor.

timeline.text: USGS and Colorado Geological Survey sources document Shamrock as a Monarch-district past producer.

sites.name: Silent Friend Mine (Chaffee County)
overview: Silent Friend is a documented Chaffee County Monarch-district mine, distinct from the Lake County namesake.

sites.name: Silver King Mine (Chaffee County)
overview: This Silver King is the Chaffee County lead mine, distinct from same-name mines elsewhere in Colorado. Mapped locality and federal mine-map records support a stable Basic Scan anchor.

timeline.text: Federal mine records preserve Silver King as a Chaffee County underground lead past producer.

sites.name: Snowflake Deposit
overview: Snowflake is a federally documented Browns Canyon fluorspar deposit developed by an adit and incline. USGS deposit mapping provides a stable Basic Scan anchor.

timeline.text: USGS Professional Paper 626 documented Snowflake and its adit/incline workings within the Browns Canyon fluorspar district.

sites.name: Stockton Mine
overview: Stockton is a significant Cleora-district copper-tungsten mine with documented shaft and adit development.

sites.name: Thirty-Six-Thirty Mine
overview: Thirty-Six-Thirty is a named Chaffee County lead-silver mine preserved in state and federal mine records. USGS topographic place mapping provides a stable Basic Scan anchor.

timeline.text: Colorado Geological Survey and federal records preserve Thirty-Six-Thirty as an underground lead-silver producer.

sites.name: Tilden Mine
overview: Tilden is a documented Chaffee County gold mine with operating-era evidence and a stable mapped mine locality.

sites.name: Tommy Evans Lode (Survey No. 14303)
overview: Tommy Evans Lode is a federally recorded silver occurrence in the Winfield district identified by Mineral Survey No. 14303.

sites.name: White King Deposit
overview: White King is a documented Browns Canyon fluorspar producer developed mainly by a long adit and shallow shaft. Federal deposit mapping supplies a stable parent-level Scan anchor.

timeline.text: White King produced fluorspar during interwar and World War II-era operating periods documented by USGS.
